note: theta/a/b for the baseline 60 bpm lead-II morphology are taken verbatim from Table I of McSharry et al. Derived morphologies state what they change and why.

afib.label: Atrial fibrillation
afib.change: P event deleted (no organised atrial depolarisation). R-R interval is randomised in cardio.ts, not here.

vt.label: Monomorphic ventricular tachycardia
vt.change: No P. QRS widened (b 0.1 -> 0.30) and made monophasic with a large discordant T, reproducing the wide-complex monomorphic morphology. Widths give a QRS duration of roughly 160 ms at 180 bpm, matching the clinical definition of a wide complex. NOTE ON AMPLITUDES: the excursion an event produces is proportional to a*b^2, so widening b without rescaling a makes the complex taller as well as wider. Keeping the published a values with a tripled b gave a 10 mV VT complex, eight times a normal R wave. These a values are set so the wide complex is about 1.5x the height of a normal R, which is what a monomorphic VT looks like.

pea.label: Pulseless electrical activity
pea.change: Electrically identical to a sinus or idioventricular complex; the defining feature is that mechanical gain is zero in cardio.ts. Complexes are broadened slightly to read as agonal.

asystole.label: Asystole
asystole.change: No events at all. The trace becomes z0 baseline wander only, which is exactly what an asystolic strip looks like: not a perfectly flat line, but a slow drift.

vfib.label: Ventricular fibrillation
vfib.model: Band-limited noise, NOT the McSharry limit cycle.

sourceRef.label: Clayton RH, Murray A, Campbell RWF. Frequency analysis of ventricular fibrillation. Eur Heart J 16(8):1112-1118, 1995.

vfib.note: VF amplitude falls with downtime; coarse VF becomes fine VF over several minutes. Half-life is our fit to the clinical observation that VF degenerates to asystole in 10-15 minutes untreated.

eeg.label: EEG band model
eeg.model: Sum of five band-limited oscillators whose relative power is set by consciousness and sedative receptor occupancy.

sourceRef.label: Schomer DL, Lopes da Silva FH (eds). Niedermeyer's Electroencephalography, 7th ed. Oxford University Press, 2017.
